title: After the storm
hookLine: Nehemiah weeps over a broken wall, rides the ruins at night, and people rebuild the stretch by their own doors
tomorrow: the Stoics distrusted feelings. which one did they keep?

cards: After a hard month, an apartment shows it: dishes, unopened mail, a plant that gave up. Nehemiah is cupbearer to the king of Persia when word reaches him that Jerusalem's wall is broken down and its gates burned.
He writes: "I sat down and wept, and mourned certain days." Then he asks the king for leave, travels to the city, and goes out by night with a few men, riding slowly along the broken wall. Looking.

teach.b: He tells no one his plan at first. He looks at the damage honestly.

teach.h: LET US RISE UP AND BUILD.
teach.b: Then he gathers the people, and they answer him, in the King James Version: "Let us rise up and build." But how do you rebuild a whole city wall?
Chapter three gives the answer, plain and clever: many repair the part nearest their own house. The priests by the horse gate, "every one over against his house." Nobody fixes everything.
Everybody fixes the piece within reach. And the book names the builders, gate by gate.
Read the list closely and there's a man named Shallum, who repaired his section, the text says, "he and his daughters."

That's the teaching Nehemiah hands down to Jews and Christians alike: a ruined place rises through many small repairs, made by people who live beside the cracks, after an honest look, and after honest weeping.
For a path of your own after a storm, the order matters. Weep first, if you need to. Then walk the damage, quietly, no speeches.
Then pick the stretch of wall in front of your own door, and start there.

how: The Book of Nehemiah, read by Jews and Christians, tells how Jerusalem's wall was rebuilt section by section, many repairing the part nearest their houses (Nehemiah 3). On a personal path, rebuilding after a hard season starts with an honest look and one small repair within reach.

games.q: after a flood, your block is a mess and the neighborhood group chat is arguing about a giant cleanup plan. what would Nehemiah's way suggest first?
o: look honestly at the damage, then each household takes the stretch nearest its door.
wait until one big crew can be hired to fix the whole block at once.
skip the grieving and the looking; just start hauling as fast as possible.
games.why: Nehemiah looked first, by night, then many repaired the part nearest their own house.

practice: Walk your own ruins in your mind, the way Nehemiah rode along the wall at night: what fell apart lately? Choose one stretch in front of your own door, one small thing to repair.
Name what might get in the way, and when you'll begin.

wordCard.voice: After the storm: the rebuilding, piece by piece. Nehemiah's city rose as people repaired the wall by their own houses.
